2607.24512.title: Making Mathematical Knowledge Explainable, Accessible and Interoperable Through Large Language Model Integration
2607.24512.paper_summary: Mathematical models are central to formalizing research problems, yet their documentation often falls short of FAIR principles. Knowledge bases such as the Mathematical Model Database (MathModDB) address this gap by providing curated, semantically rich representations of mathematical models. Built on Wikibase, the same open-source infrastructure underlying Wikidata, MathModDB utilizes Semantic Web technologies to support Linked Open Data, collaborative editing, and the storage of semantically enriched metadata, making it a domain-specific knowledge graph within the broader Wikidata ecosystem. However, access to MathModDB currently requires either navigating a complex web interface or proficiency in SPARQL and Wikibase APIs, posing significant barriers for potential users. In addition, the combination of such curated knowledge bases with actual research data stored, e.g., in Dataverse repository instances, remains a challenge. To overcome these limitations, we propose integrating Large Language Models (LLMs) with MathModDB via a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that exposes a vector-indexed schema retrieval and Steiner-tree-based join planner, combining dialogue-based natural language interaction with curated, epistemically grounded knowledge. Although instantiated on MathModDB, the architecture can be applied to other Wikibase-based systems. We demonstrate that this approach enables epistemically grounded LLM usage, improves model explainability and accessibility beyond what the standard Wikibase interface offers, and simplifies interoperability with external databases and tools, such as Dataverse data repositories. We illustrate the benefits of combining the accessibility of an LLM with the epistemic safety of a curated knowledge base through the adaptability of the MCP protocol by two use cases involving mathematical models in the fields of continuum mechanics and enzyme kinetics.
2607.24512.paper_summary_zh: 數學模型在形式化研究問題中占據核心地位，但它們的文檔往往不符合 FAIR 原則。像數學模型數據庫 (MathModDB) 這樣的知識庫通過提供經過策劃、語義豐富的數學模型表示來填補這一空白。MathModDB 建立在 Wikibase 之上，這是支撐 Wikidata 的同一開源基礎設施，利用語義網技術來支持鏈接開放數據、協作編輯以及存儲語義增強的元數據，使其成為更廣泛的 Wikidata 生態系統中的一個特定領域知識圖譜。然而，目前訪問 MathModDB 需要導航一個複雜的網絡界面或具備 SPARQL 和 Wikibase API 的熟練程度，這對潛在用戶構成了重大障礙。此外，這些策劃的知識庫與實際研究數據（例如存儲在 Dataverse 存儲庫實例中的數據）之間的結合仍然是一個挑戰。為了克服這些限制，我們提出通過模型上下文協議 (MCP) 服務器將大型語言模型 (LLMs) 與 MathModDB 集成，該服務器暴露了一個向量索引的模式檢索和基於 Steiner 樹的聯接規劃器，將基於對話的自然語言交互與策劃的、認識論上有根據的知識相結合。雖然該架構是在 MathModDB 上實現的，但可以應用於其他基於 Wikibase 的系統。我們證明這種方法使得認識論上有根據的 LLM 使用成為可能，改善了模型的可解釋性和可訪問性，超出了標準 Wikibase 界面的提供，並簡化了與外部數據庫和工具（如 Dataverse 數據存儲庫）的互操作性。我們通過兩個涉及連續介質力學和酶動力學領域的數學模型的用例，展示了將 LLM 的可訪問性與策劃知識庫的認識論安全性相結合的好處，通過 MCP 協議的適應性。
